idiom_name: unittest.mock Mock(spec=...) / create_autospec over the service class
implementation_notes: The standard library supplies the whole pattern: Mock(spec=PriceService) refuses attributes the real class does not have, create_autospec goes further and checks call signatures so a mismatched argument list raises TypeError, and return_value plus side_effect provide canned data and scripted failures. patch() swaps the object at the import site, which is the selection seam inside a test module. A hand-written fake class implementing the same protocol is still the better answer when the stand-in must behave (in-memory lookup, invariants) or when it has to be reused outside the tests.
code_sketch:
from unittest.mock import create_autospec

prices = create_autospec(PriceService)          # signatures are enforced
prices.price.return_value = Money(9, 99)

checkout = Checkout(prices)                     # client holds the contract
assert checkout.total("A-1", 2) == Money(19, 98)
prices.price.assert_called_once_with("A-1")     # optional interaction check
pitfalls: A bare Mock() without a spec accepts any attribute and any argument list, so the test agrees with a contract that no longer exists; pass spec, spec_set or use create_autospec.
patch() targets the name where the object is looked up, not where it is defined: patching the defining module leaves the importing module's binding untouched and the test calls the real code.
A mock records every call, so a stand-in reused across tests carries call history into the next test and assert_called_once fails for someone else's call.

variants.name: Hand-written fake class implementing the same methods
variants.implementation_notes: A short class with a dictionary and explicit failure behaviour is the durable option: it can carry invariants, be reused as an offline mode, and its calls are inspectable without a mocking framework. Use it when the stand-in must behave; use create_autospec when you only need answers and recorded calls.
pitfalls: A hand-written fake drifts from the real class unless something checks it: keep a shared conformance test that runs both implementations through the same cases.
Returning mutable fixture objects lets the client mutate shared state across tests; return copies or immutable values.
